sourceVersion: FDA, "Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality Management System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions", issued February 3, 2026 (supersedes June 27, 2025). Docket FDA-2021-D-1158, GUI00001825. Sections V.A.2, V.A.4(a), V.A.4(b) and VII.C.3. US Government work. Secondary source NOT vendored in this repo: the minimum elements are NTIA, "The Minimum Elements For a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)", July 12, 2021 (https://www.ntia.gov/files/ntia/publications/sbom_minimum_elements_report.pdf), which FDA incorporates by reference. FDA's own sentence names a different NTIA document, "Framing Software Component Transparency", and dates it October 2021.
notVendored: FDA incorporates the NTIA 2021 minimum elements by reference rather than enumerating them. The seven element NAMES used in item fda.sbom.ntia-minimum-elements's evidence lines therefore come from NTIA, "The Minimum Elements For a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)", July 12, 2021 (https://www.ntia.gov/files/ntia/publications/sbom_minimum_elements_report.pdf), which is not vendored under data/sources/ and so is not covered by the verbatim-excerpt traceability test. What IS traceable, and what that item's sourceExcerpt proves, is that FDA requires an SBOM consistent with those elements. Note that FDA's sentence cites a different NTIA document by title — "Framing Software Component Transparency", which FDA dates October 2021 — while asking for the "minimum elements" the July 2021 report sets out. Both are named above rather than one being silently preferred.
